germany_elec_price_setting_tip2: The EPEX spot price is quoted as a net price (excluding VAT). Therefore, the standard conversion coefficient is 1.19 (19% VAT). However, please refer to your electricity contract: if your contract includes a percentage-based adjustment on EPEX, this adjustment must first be applied and then multiplied by 1.19 to obtain the final coefficient.By correctly setting this coefficient, we can optimize the charging and discharging of your energy storage system based on your actual expenditure and electricity price, ensuring maximum benefits for you.
germany_elec_price_setting_tip4: In a dynamic electricity contract, the total price typically consists of three components:

germany_elec_price_setting_tip8: For system configuration, we recommend that you enter the costs related to Netznutzungsentgelte, taxes, levies, surcharges, and renewable energy certificates.The total of these items is referred to as the surcharge. germany_elec_price_setting_tip9: Please always refer to your actual electricity bill, as Vertriebskostenaufschlag and Netznutzungsentgelte vary depending on your supplier and region.
germany_trading_price_setting_tip2: The electricity price for ENTSO-E is a net price (netto) before tax, so the commonly used conversion factor is 1.19 (including 19% VAT). But be sure to refer to your electricity contract: if the contract includes a percentage adjustment based on ENTSO-E, apply this adjustment first, then multiply by 1.19 as the final coefficient. By correctly setting this coefficient, we can more precisely control the charging and discharging of the energy storage system based on your actual expenses and real electricity prices, thereby safeguarding your returns.
invalid_time_segment_tip: There is an invalid time period.
price_information_source_save_tooltip: The electricity prices we obtain through ENTSO-E (European Electricity Transparency Platform) are market <highlight>prices</highlight>, which are traded in the electricity market and typically fluctuate with fluctuations in market demand and supply. However, please note that the price you ultimately see on your utility bill is usually the <highlight>settlement price</highlight>, which may differ significantly from the market rate. Settlement electricity prices usually include many additional fees, such as transportation fees, distribution fees, taxes, and so on. This means that although you can optimize the charging and discharging timing of energy storage systems through the dynamic market price data we provide, the actual electricity cost may differ from the market price. We recommend that you consider this difference when using this app and verify the actual settlement price with your electricity provider to make the best energy storage decision.
price_information_source_tooltip:
ENTSO-E is the European Network of Transmission System Operators for Electricity. Its Transparency Platform publishes wholesale day-ahead prices for every European bidding zone.

2. What is a Bidding Zone?

A bidding zone is the geographic area within which the wholesale electricity price is uniform. Most countries are a single zone; a few — Sweden, Italy, Norway, Denmark — span multiple zones and let you pick the one matching your address.

3. Day-Ahead Prices

Hourly prices for the next day are published around 13:00 CET. AlphaESS uses these prices to optimize when your system charges, exports, or holds energy.
